about: The four sectors' backdrops, each for a field 72 by 40 units and for one 40 by 72, in field units from the field's top left corner, y down, back to front: a far wash, stars, one landmark, the sector's air and a vignette. Its marks reach past the field's edges, so whatever shows it clips it to the field. stars are the same for every sector at a seed: each lies at shares u and v of the field's width and height, with a radius in field units and a shine, and a field shows the first of each depth, as many as shown says; they take the field's muted text with a little of starTint, by starShares. A mark is one of: soft, an ellipse of a tint fading to nothing from its middle, turned by degrees; flat, a polygon of something hard, toned by how brightly the light falls on it, 0.3 to a little over 1; line, a thin line through points; speck, a star that stays with the landmark; streak, a hair of wind fading at both ends; or bank, billows of cloud, back to front, each hiding what is behind it. A tint names what the mark mixes into the field: a role of the palette, a rock's ink or a pilot's, and never more of it than limits allows for the palette's mode, times its strength. A mark that is fine is left out under 9 pixels a unit; one that shows in one mode is left out in the other; one that flickers brightens for a moment, every so many seconds. wind is how the air drifts, in units a second, and parallax how far each depth slides for each unit the pod flies.
